questionText: Solve the equation $2\sin^2\theta + \sin\theta - 1 = 0$ for $0° \leq \theta \leq 360°$. Give all solutions in degrees.
markingScheme:
Recognise the equation is quadratic in $\sin\theta$ **(1 mark)**
Factor as $(2\sin\theta - 1)(\sin\theta + 1) = 0$ **(2 marks)**
Solve $\sin\theta = \tfrac{1}{2}$: $\theta = 30°, 150°$ **(1 mark)**
Solve $\sin\theta = -1$: $\theta = 270°$ **(1 mark)**

solutionSteps.explanation: $\sin\theta$ is positive in quadrants I and II. Reference angle is $30°$, so $\theta = 30°$ or $\theta = 180° - 30° = 150°$.
$\sin\theta = -1$ only at $\theta = 270°$ within the given range.
